title: Full tup. Full throb.
html_source:
This chapter is highly sexual throughout, animal and sensual imagery spices this section of the book. The barmaids, Martha, Molly etc. seem to be sirens luring the men and seducing them with their feminine wiles. The men, Bloom, Lenehan etc. seem almost drunken and out of control with animalistic lust and desire.
‘Full tup. Full throb.’
Tup in British English refers to a male sheep; ram also it refers to the head of a falling hammerlike mechanism, as of a steam hammer or pile driver. Finally as a verb it is used in reference to a ram copulating with a ewe. Full throb obviously is a way of writing about the engorged male member. This whole section and many that follow are about desire for sex, wanton lust.
